title: Lucky Thompson, Willie Anderson and the young altos
summary: Meeting Lucky Thompson and the pack of young Detroit altos, with his grandmother pulling him back and forth to Jackson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: During this period I met the great saxophonist, Lucky Thompson. He was just coming out of high school. And I had entered school. I had entered Northern for a while. But my grandmother always had me going back and forth between Detroit and Jackson. Because when she got ready to come to Detroit, she didn't care whether I was going to school or not. I'd have to drive back to Jackson and ride back up with her, and ride back up with her, and take her back, and then come back to Detroit! So I began to lose out in school a little bit...

Yeah, there were so many great players around Detroit during that time. They had an excellent pianist named Willie Anderson. He was terrific. And I also met Rudy Rutherford, who was a fine clarinetist, around that time. He was from Detroit. And we were like the young alto players around there -- Bernie Peacock, Sonny Stitt, Rudy Rutherford. And then Wardell came to town, Wardell Gray, when he came to town playing alto he was added to the list. So we had a lot of young saxophone players on the scene.
My gigs were picking up more and more, as I got better known around the city.
